topics: Dedicated vs hosted for EU region
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-25 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~58m | Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Maya (CSM), Jordan (Eng Ops); Priya (VP ML), Liam (Head Platform), Nina (Procurement), Aaron (CTO), Ravi (SRE).

Summary: short readout at top, see notes — main objective: finalize scope for renewal amendment (EU region + committed capacity) and agree next validation steps.

00:00:00 Sofia: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, uh this is Sofia from Redwood, i left the agenda in the calendar but quick intro round.
00:00:12 Priya: thanks Sofia, i'm Priya. we'll jump straight in, have about an hour.
00:00:18 Ethan: hi all, Ethan here, i'll cover the benchmarking plan and canary ideas.
00:00:25 Liam: Liam here, platform lead. main ask: we want minimal user impact while we flip traffic to eu nodes.
00:00:32 Sofia: perfect. so high level — the renewal window is coming up and you mentioned wanting to add eu-west region plus a committed GPU pool, correct?
00:00:45 Priya: yeah that's right. we have production traffic in us-east but European customers are ramping in q2. ideally we want eu-region live before April.
00:00:56 Nina: and procurement wants clarity on billing cadence, cancellation terms, and a clear SLA uplift if we move to dedicated.
00:01:06 Sofia: understood. quick clarification — are you leaning dedicated capacity in EU or hosted with reserved burst?
00:01:14 Liam: leaning dedicated for predictable latency and data controls, but cost is the hangup. if the metrics say p95 latency under 120ms for our 1k token gen, that could justify it.
00:01:26 Ethan: ok note — 1k tokens is a decent size, we'll need to benchmark both quantized variants and the full fp16 path; quantization tradeoffs might reduce cost but can change output quality slightly.
00:01:38 Aaron: quality is non-negotiable for clinical summaries, we can't tolerate hallucination regressions.
00:01:44 Priya: yep and audit logs / key management are mandatory. do you support customer-managed KMS in Private and in Dedicated?
00:01:53 Jordan: short answer — Dedicated supports customer KMS/HSM; Hosted we can integrate via an encrypted envelope, but full KMS control is only on Private or Dedicated with VPC peering.
00:02:06 Ravi: ok that helps. we need to capture egress constraints — our security folks restrict cross-border data. what are options for data residency?
00:02:14 Sofia: we have EU-dedicated clusters and Private VPC paths; we can set region pinning so requests stay within eu-west. also we log token-level traces per route for audits.
00:02:28 Priya: great. on the timing and cost — Nina, procurement wants a one-pager with sample numbers broken out: committed GPUs, overage rates, and sample monthly bill with expected RPS.
00:02:39 Nina: yes. and is there a minimum notice for scaling down? we've seen lock-in concerns.
00:02:46 Maya: operational note — we support tiered commitments with a 30-day notice window on the committed pool, and a 60-day term if you want lower rates; i'll put the exact language in the amendment.
00:02:58 Sofia: to avoid downtime, Ethan proposed a canary rollout pattern. Ethan can you walk us through the plan?
00:03:06 Ethan: sure. plan is: baseline — keep us-east as primary; deploy eu cluster in parallel, run synthetic traffic at 0% production, snapshot KV cache patterns, then do a 1% traffic split, monitor latency/error/quality, then 10%, 50% and final cutover. each step waits on SLOs and quality checks.
00:03:25 Liam: can we warm the KV cache so first requests don't spike latency?
00:03:29 Ethan: yes — we can pre-warm with prefix caching, and we support continuous batching which helps flatten latency spikes during warmup.
00:03:37 Ravi: will there be cross-region cache misses impacting cost? if requests are pinned, cache is local; but during the ramp we might see thundering misses.
00:03:44 Ethan: good point — we'll budget for a warmup delta; our estimate is an initial 10-15% token cost uplift for the first 48 hours. we'll capture that in the amendment as expected transient usage.
00:03:57 Priya: that's helpful, we need that number to forecast.
00:04:02 Sofia: on SLA — Dedicated gives you a latency SLO target and higher availability SLA. Maya will add precise SLA metrics to the doc.
00:04:09 Maya: yes i'll include p95 latency targets and a 99.9% uptime baseline for the committed pool.
00:04:14 Nina: do you have SOC 2 / ISO attestations we can share?
00:04:18 Sofia: absolutely — we'll attach the security pack (SOC 2 report, ISO summary, encryption and KMS architecture).
00:04:24 Priya: excellent.

00:08:10 Ethan: (benchmark deep-dive) so for the synthetic run we'll mirror your token distribution — you said an average 900-1100 tokens per gen?
00:08:18 Priya: yes around 1k tokens. peak 60 rps during business hours. sustained 20 rps off-peak.
00:08:25 Ethan: ok we'll run 50 rps steady for 30 minutes and 1 minute spikes to 80 to observe p95/p99. we'll test both a quantized 8-bit path and the fp16 path; we'll provide latency, cpu/gpu utilization, and token cost per 1k output.
00:08:39 Liam: what about fallback policy? if eu cluster degrades, do we route back to us-east? that's acceptable provided data residency controls are intact.
00:08:47 Jordan: we can configure smart routing policies: by default route eu-origin requests to eu cluster; fallback route allowed only for non-personally-identifiable requests, and we can tag routes to block fallback for sensitive flows.
00:08:59 Priya: ok that's important. we'll need route level flags for PHI vs non-PHI.
00:09:06 Sofia: noted. we'll include that in the security checklist.

00:20:05 Aaron: quick question on billing — if we commit to a 6-GPU pool, can we burst beyond that and how are overages billed?
00:20:13 Sofia: overages are billed at the burst rate per GPU-hour listed in appendix A; we can also add a monthly overage cap if desired.
00:20:20 Nina: can you do a blended pricing example for 6 vs 12 GPUs over a 12-month term? procurement prefers line items.
00:20:27 Sofia: yes i'll produce a table — 6-commitment gives X discounted rate, 12 gives further discount but a 24-month commitment opens more savings. i'll include sample monthly invoices.
00:20:38 Priya: another onboarding risk — model drift after quantization. can Redwood run regen tests to compare outputs? we need quality regressions flagged.
00:20:47 Ethan: we've got an eval harness; we can run side-by-side rollouts with prompt sets you provide and flag token-level deltas and rouge/semantic metrics. we'll make a quality gate for the canary steps.
00:20:58 Priya: great. provide the eval metrics format so we can include them in our approval flow.

00:32:15 Liam: from an infra perspective, we need a network diagram and port/IP allowlist details. who sends that?
00:32:20 Jordan: i'll send a minimal diagram and the allowlist template. we'll need your egress and firewall restrictions.
00:32:28 Ravi: we may have to run Private in eu due to regulatory needs for certain customers; is that a separate procurement line?
00:32:35 Sofia: Private is a separate contract — we can discuss a roadmap: start with Dedicated (faster), then move to Private if/when you need full on-prem or air-gapped. we can reflect that optionality in the amendment.
00:32:49 Priya: timeline check — April is our target. is that feasible?
00:32:53 Ethan: yes if we start benchmark and sign amendment by end of Feb, we can schedule cluster provisioning in early March and do a staged ramp in March-April.
00:33:01 Sofia: key gating items: signed amendment, network allowlist, KMS requirements, model vetting prompts. once those are in, we give you a provisioning ETA.

00:41:02 Nina: a question on termination and scale-down — if usage falls below committed level, do we auto-bill or prorate?
00:41:09 Maya: commitments are billed monthly per the committed tier; we can include a 30-day adjustment window for downscaling with prorated credits for future months. i'll include specific language.
00:41:20 Nina: that's good. procurement will want that.

00:47:14 Priya: what's the expected transient cost during the warmup again? you said 10-15% token uplift, but translate that to dollars for our volumes (roughly 500M tokens/month).
00:47:24 Ethan: rough calc — at your current per-token effective rate, a 12% uplift on 500M tokens is about X thousand dollars a month; Sofia will include a worked example with the amendment. (note: rough, will confirm in spreadsheet)
00:47:39 Sofia: yes we'll give numbers in the amendment spreadsheet, including committed vs blended vs burst cost.

00:53:02 Aaron: last thing — if we opt for a 24-month term for better pricing, can we get quarterly review checkpoints tied to usage adjustments?
00:53:10 Sofia: absolutely. we can add a quarterly business review cadence and a usage smoothing clause tied to reasonable ramp schedules.
00:53:18 Priya: ok that sounds reasonable.

00:56:00 Sofia: recap and next steps — i will: 1) draft the commitment amendment with 2 capacity options (6 GPU vs 12 GPU) and 12/24 month pricing, 2) attach security pack (SOC2/ISO/KMS details), 3) include billable warmup delta and sample invoice examples. Ethan will run the synthetic benchmark and share raw and summarized results. Jordan will send network diagram template. Maplebridge to confirm term preference and internal approvals.
00:56:22 Priya: timeline accepted. we'll aim to finalize procurement decisions by Jan 30.
00:56:30 Sofia: great. any final questions?
00:56:34 Ravi: none from me. thanks.
00:56:36 Nina: thanks all.
00:56:40 Ethan: thanks. we'll follow up on the benchmark link.
00:56:45 Sofia: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-attributions and filler (um, yeah). References: security pack link (redwood.com/security-pack), amendment draft link (redwood.com/amendments/CRM-789230-draft), benchmark result placeholder (s3://redwood-benchmarks/ff-20260125-mbh).
